methodology.reconstructed_daily: Source-backed historical editorial reconstruction produced later; not a contemporaneously published assessment.
methodology.verified_event: Primary-source policy or trade event aligned to its first market session.
methodology.objective_market_reconstruction: Rule-based reconstruction from contemporaneous market-price/rate changes; not a retroactive claim about the day’s news narrative.

catalysts.title: 胡塞袭击沙特能源设施并推动Brent升至99.00美元，海湾风险由航运摩擦升级为新的实物供给冲击
catalysts.evidence: 沙特官方通报称南部多处能源设施遭袭，部分设施起火且部分运营临时中断；Reuters报道共有73人受伤，Brent升至99.00美元、盘中最高99.22美元，WTI升至94.41美元。
catalysts.transmission: 沙特设施中断 → 原油/柴油风险溢价 → 通胀预期 → 美债收益率与Fed路径 → 股票久期和信用条件。
catalysts.confirmation: Brent维持99–100美元上方，同时美国现金市场重开后美债收益率与波动率同步上升，才算确认商品冲击已经扩散为金融条件收紧。
catalysts.invalidation: 沙特运营快速恢复、替代路线吸收损失，且Brent回落至袭击前区间，同时收益率和波动率不再上行，则本轮冲击更接近短期风险溢价。

catalysts.title: 中国8月出口同比增长25.0%、进口增长28.2%，顺差1190.9亿美元但外需强于内需的结构仍未消失
catalysts.evidence: 中国8月美元计价出口同比增长25.0%，与Reuters调查预期一致；进口增长28.2%，低于30%的预期，贸易顺差扩大至1190.9亿美元，同时原油进口量同比下降23.4%。
catalysts.transmission: 中国贸易结构 → CNH/铜/亚洲周期股 → 中国增长预期 → 商品需求与区域风险偏好。
catalysts.confirmation: CNH保持稳定、铜和亚洲周期股持续走强，且后续国内需求指标显示进口强势并非主要由价格效应造成，才算确认增长端改善更全面。
catalysts.invalidation: CNH走弱、周期股冲高回落，或后续数据证明进口增长主要来自价格而非数量，则强出口难以改变内需偏弱的核心叙事。

catalysts.title: USDJPY盘中触及152.89且日元较上周初升值约4%，BOJ收紧预期进入全球carry unwind实盘压力测试
catalysts.evidence: 日元兑美元盘中升至152.89，为约七个月最强水平，随后伦敦早盘回到154附近；Reuters称日元较上周初累计升值约4%，BOJ加息预期、资金回流与套息仓位回补共同推动。
catalysts.transmission: BOJ加息/资金回流预期 → JPY升值 → carry去杠杆 → 日本与全球股票/波动率 → 跨境久期资金流。
catalysts.confirmation: USDJPY持续低于此前155附近，同时股票或信用波动率随日元进一步升值而上行，说明去杠杆已经超出单纯FX重定价。
catalysts.invalidation: USDJPY快速回到155–157上方，且全球风险资产与日元脱钩，则更可能是有序仓位调整而非广谱去杠杆。

days.regime_label: Event Risk / Physical Supply + Global Tightening

catalysts.title: 海湾与阿曼湾多艘商船遭 disabling fire，Brent突破100美元并把航运风险升级为实物供给压力
catalysts.evidence: Reuters援引英国海事贸易行动办公室与海事安全来源报道，海湾和阿曼湾北部多艘商业船只在夜间遭 disabling fire 并受损；至少一艘船在迪拜Port Rashid附近倾侧，暂未确认人员伤亡或环境影响。与此同时美国已摧毁五艘伊朗原油运输船，伊朗方面继续声称攻击美军舰与油轮。
catalysts.transmission: 商船受损/航线受限 → 运费与保险上升、出口可用性下降 → Brent/柴油风险溢价上升 → 通胀预期与长端收益率抬升 → 风险资产折现率和信用条件收紧。
catalysts.confirmation: 若Brent持续站上100美元且海事安全机构继续报告商业航运受损、Hormuz通行量进一步下降，同时10Y/VIX上行，将确认实体供给冲击正在扩散。
catalysts.invalidation: 若后续没有新增商业航运损失、航线流量恢复且Brent重新跌回100美元下方并伴随运费和保险风险溢价回落，则冲击更可能维持为事件性溢价。

catalysts.title: 中国8月CPI同比升至0.8%、PPI同比升至3.8%，能源与金属成本开始更清晰进入制造业价格
catalysts.evidence: 中国国家统计局公布，8月CPI同比上涨0.8%、环比上涨0.4%，扣除食品和能源的核心CPI同比上涨1.0%；PPI同比上涨3.8%、环比上涨0.4%，燃料动力类购进价格同比上涨9.8%，有色金属材料及电线类上涨19.8%。
catalysts.transmission: 能源/金属成本上升 → 中国PPI与企业投入成本上升 → 出口与工业品价格压力 → 全球商品/制造业通胀 → 央行宽松空间收窄。
catalysts.confirmation: 若未来PPI、出口价格或企业利润率继续体现能源与金属成本传导，同时CNH与亚洲利率上行，则成本推动链条得到确认。
catalysts.invalidation: 若后续核心CPI、PPI和购进价格快速回落，且制造业利润不受能源成本明显挤压，则本轮上行更可能是短期商品价格冲击。

catalysts.title: USDJPY约153.05且日本10年期JGB近期触及3%，BOJ加息与国内资金回流继续挤压全球carry trade
catalysts.evidence: 美元兑日元在欧洲时段约153.05，较9月1日约160水平显著回落；Reuters同时报道日本10年期国债收益率近期触及3%，为1996年以来首次，Fitch认为持续通胀可能推动BOJ更快加息并加速国内保险、养老金资金回流。
catalysts.transmission: BOJ加息/JGB收益率上升 → 日本资金回流 + JPY升值 → 海外债券边际需求下降与carry平仓 → 全球长端收益率和高beta资产波动上升。
catalysts.confirmation: 若USDJPY继续下行、JGB收益率维持高位且日本机构海外债券需求走弱，同时美债长端与高beta资产承压，将确认回流与carry unwind扩散。
catalysts.invalidation: 若BOJ收紧预期回落、JGB收益率回落且USDJPY重新稳定走高，全球资产对日本资金回流的敏感度将下降。

days.regime_label: Event Risk / Two-Chokepoint Energy + Global Rates Tightening

catalysts.title: Houthis seize Mocha and reach Hanish islands, pushing Brent above $105 before the 18:00 SGT cutoff
catalysts.evidence: Reuters reported before the historical cutoff that Houthi forces seized Yemen's Red Sea port of Mocha and reached the Hanish islands area, threatening a route Saudi Arabia increasingly relied on while Hormuz traffic was impaired; Brent rose above $105 per barrel intraday.
catalysts.transmission: Bab el-Mandeb + Hormuz disruption → shipping/export capacity → Brent/diesel → inflation expectations → global yields → equity and credit multiples.
catalysts.confirmation: Further verified disruption to Red Sea or Hormuz transit, sustained crude above the pre-cutoff highs, or continued evidence that Gulf exports remain materially below normal.
catalysts.invalidation: Verified de-escalation and restoration of commercial transit through at least one chokepoint that lowers shipping costs and pulls crude back toward the prior range.

catalysts.title: Global bond yields jump as oil shock deepens, with UK 10Y gilts at 5.378% ahead of ECB and U.S. PPI
catalysts.evidence: Reuters reported UK 10-year gilt yields at 5.378%, their highest since 2007, while 20-year and 30-year yields reached roughly 5.895% and 5.948%, the highest since 1998, as oil traded above $105 and investors awaited the still-unreleased ECB decision and U.S. PPI.
catalysts.transmission: Oil shock → inflation/term premium → UK/EU/U.S. long yields → global discount rates → duration assets and credit spreads.
catalysts.confirmation: Post-event rate markets continue to hold near or above the pre-cutoff highs and equity duration underperforms as the oil shock persists.
catalysts.invalidation: Soft inflation evidence or clearly dovish central-bank guidance drives a sustained global yield reversal despite still-elevated oil.

catalysts.title: BOJ board member Masu says rapid rate hikes may be needed if inflation accelerates, reinforcing September tightening risk
catalysts.evidence: BOJ board member Kazuyuki Masu said the central bank might need to raise rates rapidly if inflation accelerates, with the policy rate at 1% and analysts expecting a possible September increase to 1.25%, reinforcing the normalization signal while USDJPY remained near 153.70.
catalysts.transmission: BOJ normalization → JPY funding cost / repatriation → carry unwind → global leverage reduction → equities, credit and duration volatility.
catalysts.confirmation: USDJPY remains materially below early-September levels, BOJ hike pricing stays elevated, and global leveraged assets weaken alongside firmer Japanese yields.
catalysts.invalidation: BOJ communication turns materially less hawkish and USDJPY retraces the recent yen rally without broader leverage stress.

catalysts.title: IEA deepens 2026 oil-supply decline to 5.7 million bpd and pushes normal Gulf flows into 2027
catalysts.evidence: IEA将2026年全球原油供应降幅扩大至570万桶/日、约6%，并指出正常中东海湾流量恢复已被推迟到2027年；8月全球库存以日均310万桶速度下降。
catalysts.transmission: Gulf supply loss → inventories → crude/diesel → inflation expectations → central-bank path → global yields and equity multiples.
catalysts.confirmation: 未来数周海湾出口仍显著低于正常水平、库存继续下降且Brent维持100美元以上，将确认供给缺口正在跨月固化。
catalysts.invalidation: 若形成可验证的航运安排、海湾出口快速恢复且库存停止下降，IEA所描述的持续性供给压力将开始减弱。

catalysts.title: Houthis reach Perim island, threatening a second major oil transit corridor at Bab el-Mandeb
catalysts.evidence: 四名也门政府消息人士向Reuters确认胡塞武装已抵达Bab el-Mandeb海峡的战略性Perim岛，并控制面向该岛的Dhubab；沙特在Hormuz受限后正更依赖红海路线。
catalysts.transmission: Perim control risk → Red Sea transit capacity/insurance → Saudi export flexibility → Brent/diesel → inflation and global rates.
catalysts.confirmation: 商业船舶改道、保险成本上升或沙特红海出口受到可验证限制，将确认第二通道风险已经进入实体供给。
catalysts.invalidation: 也门政府重新控制Perim/Dhubab或红海商业通行维持正常且运费回落，将削弱第二通道风险溢价。

catalysts.title: U.S. August CPI at 08:30 EDT becomes the next rate-path test with 10Y yields near 5%
catalysts.evidence: 美国8月CPI尚未在research_cutoff前公布；Reuters调查显示核心CPI环比预期中心约为0.2%，而Fed下周加息25bp的市场概率已升至约67%至70%。
catalysts.transmission: CPI surprise → Fed September pricing → UST 2Y/10Y → DXY → Nasdaq/Russell and global duration assets.
catalysts.confirmation: CPI高于预期且2Y/10Y收益率重新上行、美元同步走强，将确认能源通胀正在进入更广泛的政策定价。
catalysts.invalidation: CPI明显低于预期并伴随2Y、10Y和美元同步回落，将首次给出可信的再通胀链反向确认。

days.regime_label: Weekend Event Risk / Reinflation + Global Tightening

catalysts.title: Saudi Arabia shuts East-West pipeline after drone attack, removing a 4–5 million bpd Hormuz bypass
catalysts.evidence: Saudi Arabia confirmed a precautionary shutdown of the 1,200-km East-West pipeline after a drone attack traced to Iraqi territory; Reuters said recent throughput was roughly 4–5 million bpd.
catalysts.transmission: Pipeline outage → higher crude/freight premium → inflation expectations → front-end yields → pressure on duration and cyclicals.
catalysts.confirmation: The line remains shut or no credible restart is confirmed while Gulf and Red Sea flows stay impaired.
catalysts.invalidation: Saudi restores meaningful East-West throughput and at least one major shipping route improves without new attacks.

catalysts.title: U.S. August CPI rises 0.4% m/m and pushes September Fed hike odds to roughly 86–90%
catalysts.evidence: August U.S. CPI rose 0.4% m/m and 3.4% y/y; core CPI rose 0.3% m/m and 2.4% y/y, while gasoline rose 3.9% and rate markets strongly priced a September hike.
catalysts.transmission: CPI acceleration → higher Fed hike probability → higher 2Y/real yields → tighter dollar liquidity and valuation compression.
catalysts.confirmation: 2Y yields hold near Friday levels and September hike pricing remains elevated despite any crude pullback.
catalysts.invalidation: Fed pricing retreats materially because energy risk reverses or incoming data weakens enough to dominate inflation.

catalysts.title: Perim seizure and record VLCC freight rates turn Middle East shipping risk into a two-chokepoint cost shock
catalysts.evidence: Perim at Bab el-Mandeb remained under Houthi control while Hormuz traffic was constrained; Gulf of Oman-to-China VLCC freight was near record levels around Worldscale 450.
catalysts.transmission: Shipping stress + record freight → higher delivered energy costs → weaker real income → higher inflation expectations and tighter policy.
catalysts.confirmation: VLCC rates stay near records, Hormuz transit remains depressed and Perim continues to constrain Bab el-Mandeb.
catalysts.invalidation: Shipping security improves, tanker availability rises and freight rates fall materially.

days.regime_label: Weekend Event Risk / Reinflation + Tight Financial Conditions

catalysts.title: Sunday Hormuz vessel strike adds a fresh physical-supply shock while Saudi Arabia's East-West bypass pipeline remains shut
catalysts.evidence: UKMTO reported a vessel transiting the Strait of Hormuz was hit by a projectile and caught fire, prompting crew evacuation; AP separately reported an Iranian commercial vessel struck near Qeshm. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, the principal land bypass around Hormuz, remained under a precautionary shutdown with no verified restart notice through the cutoff.
catalysts.transmission: Dual-route physical constraint → crude/freight premium → inflation expectations → Fed and term premium → global yields and equity multiples.
catalysts.confirmation: A persistent crude gap higher after Globex reopens, tighter tanker/freight conditions or further verified infrastructure/vessel damage would confirm the shock remains binding.
catalysts.invalidation: A verified Saudi pipeline restart plus stable Hormuz flows and a rapidly fading crude gap would weaken the immediate physical-supply thesis.

catalysts.title: Saudi equities register the first traded Sunday reaction to pipeline attacks, with TASI down 1.0% and Aramco down 1.1%
catalysts.evidence: Reuters reported Saudi Arabia's benchmark TASI fell 1.0% on Sunday after drone attacks on the East-West oil pipeline; Al Rajhi Bank fell 0.8%, Ma'aden 2.4%, Saudi Aramco 1.1% and Rabigh Refining 7.3%.
catalysts.transmission: Pipeline attack → Saudi equity/credit risk premium → regional funding confidence → energy and global risk sentiment into Monday futures.
catalysts.confirmation: Continued weakness in Saudi energy/financial shares and a matching risk-off move in oil-sensitive global assets after futures reopen would confirm cross-market transmission.
catalysts.invalidation: A quick local equity recovery combined with stable crude and no further infrastructure disruption would suggest the Sunday drop was a contained event premium.

catalysts.title: Yen speculators flip net long for the first time since February, adding an independent carry-unwind channel to the energy shock
catalysts.evidence: Reuters reported CFTC data showing speculative yen positions swung to 10,796 contracts net long in the week to September 8 from 92,227 net short previously, the first net-long stance since February 24; USDJPY had reached 152.89 during that week.
catalysts.transmission: Yen appreciation / BOJ normalization → higher funding cost → carry reduction → cross-asset deleveraging → tighter financial conditions.
catalysts.confirmation: Further yen strength after Monday reopen accompanied by weakness in high-beta equities or widening funding-sensitive spreads would confirm the carry channel.
catalysts.invalidation: A durable USDJPY rebound with stable global risk assets and no further BOJ tightening repricing would weaken the near-term carry-unwind signal.

catalysts.title: Oman postpones Monday Hormuz talks as Brent jumps back above $107 with Saudi's East–West pipeline still offline
catalysts.evidence: Oman's foreign minister confirmed that the Gulf states–Iran meeting planned for Monday to discuss the Strait of Hormuz was postponed without a new date. At the same time, Saudi Arabia had not announced a restart of the East–West pipeline, which Reuters said recently rerouted about 4 million barrels per day, while Brent rose 2.6% to $107.36 and WTI 2.4% to $102.48 in Asian trading.
catalysts.transmission: Diplomacy setback + impaired bypass capacity → crude/freight premium → inflation expectations → Fed/term premium → global yields and equity multiples.
catalysts.confirmation: Brent holding above $107 through Europe/U.S. trading, no verified Saudi pipeline restart and further shipping disruption would confirm the supply premium remains binding.
catalysts.invalidation: A verified partial/full East–West pipeline restart, a rescheduled Hormuz framework with broad participation and a sustained crude reversal below Friday levels would weaken the immediate thesis.

catalysts.title: Monday Asia delivers the first broad risk-off confirmation: Nikkei -1.7%, Korea -3.3% and Nasdaq futures -1.1%
catalysts.evidence: The Monday session translated the weekend energy shock into equities: Reuters reported Japan's Nikkei down 1.7%, South Korea's benchmark down 3.3%, S&P 500 futures down 0.5% and Nasdaq futures down 1.1%. The U.S. 10-year yield remained close to 5% at 4.967%, limiting the valuation cushion for growth stocks.
catalysts.transmission: Higher oil + high sovereign yields → weaker Asia equities and U.S. futures → wider volatility/risk premium → tighter financial conditions.
catalysts.confirmation: A weak U.S. cash open with VIX higher and growth/semiconductor underperformance while crude stays firm would confirm broadening stress.
catalysts.invalidation: A rapid U.S. equity recovery, falling VIX and oil fading despite unchanged supply facts would suggest the Asia move was primarily opening-gap risk.

catalysts.title: Fed and BOJ hike probabilities converge in the same week while yen strength keeps the carry-unwind channel active
catalysts.evidence: Markets price roughly an 86% chance of a 25bp Fed hike this week and about a 76% chance of a 25bp BOJ hike to 1.25%. USDJPY traded near 153.49 on Monday after the yen's sharp September rally, and CFTC data showed speculators flipped net long yen for the first time since February.
catalysts.transmission: Hot inflation + BOJ normalization → higher front-end rates / stronger yen → carry reduction and higher discount rates → pressure on high-beta and long-duration assets.
catalysts.confirmation: Fed/BOJ hike probabilities staying high, USDJPY testing or breaking the 152.89 recent low and front-end yields holding elevated would confirm the channel.
catalysts.invalidation: Materially softer U.S. data, a Fed pause repricing or BOJ guidance that removes follow-on tightening would reduce the dual-policy shock.

catalysts.title: Saudi East–West pipeline remains offline as fresh Houthi attacks keep Brent above $106
catalysts.evidence: Reuters reported Brent at $106.93 and WTI at $102.65 in Tuesday Asian trading while Saudi Arabia's East–West pipeline remained offline after attacks; the route had recently rerouted roughly 4 million barrels per day, about 4% of global supply.
catalysts.transmission: Pipeline outage + constrained Hormuz traffic → crude/freight premium → inflation expectations → central-bank tightening → higher yields and lower equity multiples.
catalysts.confirmation: Brent staying above $106 through Europe/U.S. trading, no verified pipeline restart and additional shipping or infrastructure attacks would confirm a persistent physical premium.
catalysts.invalidation: A verified East–West restart, materially improved Hormuz transit and a sustained crude reversal toward pre-weekend levels would weaken the supply-shock thesis.

catalysts.title: Fed begins its September meeting with a 25bp hike now the dominant call and the U.S. 10Y testing 5%
catalysts.evidence: The Federal Reserve's September 15-16 meeting begins Tuesday. Reuters' latest economist poll has a 25bp hike to 3.75%-4.00% as the majority call, while the 10-year Treasury yield crossed 5% on Monday for the first time since 2023.
catalysts.transmission: Fed decision + projections → front-end path/term premium → U.S. dollar and 10Y → global funding costs → equity/credit valuations.
catalysts.confirmation: A 25bp hike accompanied by a higher projected path, firm inflation language and 10Y yields holding near or above 5% would confirm sustained tightening.
catalysts.invalidation: A hold or a hike paired with clearly limited follow-through, falling long-end yields and a softer dollar would weaken the tightening-extension thesis.

catalysts.title: China August activity data due at 10:00 SGT after bank lending rebounded to only 60 billion yuan
catalysts.evidence: China is due to release August industrial output, retail sales and fixed-asset investment shortly after this research cutoff. A current economic calendar points to roughly 4.8% industrial growth, 0.8% retail growth and a deeper year-to-date investment contraction, after August new bank loans reached only 60 billion yuan versus a 400 billion yuan Reuters-polled expectation.
catalysts.transmission: China activity surprise → CNH/China equities → copper and regional cyclicals → global growth expectations → commodity and risk-asset breadth.
catalysts.confirmation: Broad weakness across industrial output, retail sales and investment alongside soft credit would confirm domestic-demand fragility.
catalysts.invalidation: A broad-based upside surprise, especially in retail and private investment proxies, would challenge the weak-domestic-demand narrative.

catalysts.title: Fed decision at 02:00 SGT tests whether a 5% U.S. 10Y becomes a durable valuation ceiling
catalysts.evidence: The FOMC decision lands today; Reuters' poll has 85% of economists expecting +25bp to 3.75%-4.00%, while Tuesday markets priced about 94.5% odds and the 10Y ended near 5.004%.
catalysts.transmission: Fed path → yields/dollar → funding costs → equity, credit and duration valuations.
catalysts.confirmation: Hawkish language with the 10Y holding around or above 5% confirms tighter conditions.
catalysts.invalidation: Limited follow-through plus falling yields and a softer dollar weakens the sustained-tightening thesis.

catalysts.title: Saudi route risk stays structural even as a surprise U.S. inventory build pushes Brent to $107.82
catalysts.evidence: Brent fell 0.86% to $107.82 and WTI 0.92% to $104.86 after API data showed crude inventories +7.1m barrels versus a 1.6m draw expected; Yanbu loadings remain suspended.
catalysts.transmission: Route risk vs inventories → crude/diesel → inflation expectations → rates → risk-asset discount rates.
catalysts.confirmation: Brent staying elevated with continued Yanbu suspension or new attacks confirms a durable premium.
catalysts.invalidation: Verified route restart plus sustained crude declines materially weakens the supply-shock thesis.

catalysts.title: Japan's 28% import jump and 19.3% export growth sharpen the BOJ trade-off before September 17–18
catalysts.evidence: Japan's August imports rose 28.0% y/y versus 26.3% expected, exports rose 19.3% versus 18.2%, and the trade deficit reached ¥1.106tn as expensive oil lifted import costs.
catalysts.transmission: Oil import bill + BOJ path → JGB/yen → carry funding → Asian equities and global leveraged growth.
catalysts.confirmation: A BOJ hike with firmer JGB yields and a stronger yen confirms tighter funding conditions.
catalysts.invalidation: A dovish hold with stable oil import costs and a weaker yen reduces the carry-unwind risk.

catalysts.title: Fed restarts tightening with a unanimous 25bp hike while the 2026 policy-rate median remains near 4.1%
catalysts.evidence: The FOMC voted 12-0 to raise the target range to 3.75%-4.00%; September projections show a 2026 median policy-rate path near 4.1%, leaving another hike consistent with the outlook.
catalysts.transmission: Fed hike → 2Y yield/dollar → borrowing cost and WACC → equity, credit and housing valuations.
catalysts.confirmation: UST 2Y staying elevated with DXY firm and funding-sensitive equities lagging would confirm persistent policy transmission.
catalysts.invalidation: A sustained fall in front-end yields and DXY with broader equity participation would weaken the renewed-tightening thesis.

catalysts.title: Saudi export workarounds via Oman cut Brent 2.7%, testing whether physical logistics can break the energy-to-rates loop
catalysts.evidence: Brent settled at $105.83, down 2.7%, and WTI at $102.43, down 3.2%, after Saudi Arabia offered more crude via ship-to-ship transfers off Sohar; U.S. crude inventories fell only 640,000 barrels.
catalysts.transmission: Alternative export capacity → crude/freight premium ↓ → inflation pressure ↓ → term premium/policy pressure ↓.
catalysts.confirmation: More verified Sohar loadings, fewer delivery disruptions and lower Brent would confirm that logistics are absorbing part of the shock.
catalysts.invalidation: Renewed route attacks, cancellations or a quick Brent rebound would show the physical constraint remains dominant.

catalysts.title: BoE today and BOJ Friday become the next test of synchronized global tightening after the Fed hike
catalysts.evidence: The BoE is due at 12:00 London today; Reuters expects a 3.75% hold. Reuters expects the BOJ to raise its policy rate to 1.25% Friday, a 31-year high.
catalysts.transmission: BoE/BOJ decisions → gilt/JGB yields and GBP/JPY → carry/funding → global duration and credit.
catalysts.confirmation: A hawkish BoE vote split plus a BOJ hike with further-normalization guidance would confirm synchronized tightening.
catalysts.invalidation: A cautious BoE hold and BOJ guidance that caps follow-on hikes would reduce the global tightening cascade risk.

catalysts.title: BOJ decision today tests whether a widely expected hike to 1.25% strengthens the yen without reigniting global duration stress
catalysts.evidence: Japan's August national core CPI rose 1.7% y/y, below the 1.8% Reuters consensus, while USDJPY traded around 156.15 and the Nikkei rose 0.8% in early Friday trade. A Reuters poll before the meeting showed economists expecting a 25bp hike to 1.25%.
catalysts.transmission: BOJ rate/guidance → JGB curve and USDJPY → yen-funded leverage → Asian/global duration and high-beta equities.
catalysts.confirmation: A BOJ hike accompanied by an orderly stronger yen and contained JGB/global long yields would confirm controlled normalization.
catalysts.invalidation: A hawkish path that drives JGB yields and yen funding costs sharply higher, or an unexpected hold that weakens the yen further, would invalidate the controlled-normalization setup.

catalysts.title: Oil falls toward $103 Brent even as Saudi pipeline damage expands to three pumping stations, separating tactical logistics relief from structural supply risk
catalysts.evidence: Reuters reported that three pumping stations on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline were damaged and several sources estimated full repairs could take five to six weeks. Yet Brent fell to about $103.74 in early Asia as partial restoration and Oman loading workarounds reduced immediate scarcity fears.
catalysts.transmission: Pipeline repair pace / alternative loadings → crude and freight premium → inflation expectations → long yields and central-bank path → risk assets.
catalysts.confirmation: Verified restoration of material East-West capacity, continued Sohar loadings and Brent holding lower would confirm that logistics are absorbing the outage.
catalysts.invalidation: Repair delays, new route attacks or a renewed Brent spike despite partial restoration would show the physical constraint remains dominant.

catalysts.title: Post-Fed risk relief broadens as U.S. equities rebound and long yields fall, but Friday quarterly expiry will test whether the move survives event-flow normalization
catalysts.evidence: The S&P 500 rose 1.14%, Nasdaq 1.69% and Russell 2000 0.55% on Thursday while the U.S. 10-year yield fell to about 4.93%. CME's calendar marks September 18 as the quarterly U.S. equity-index futures expiration date.
catalysts.transmission: Lower oil/yields + event uncertainty cleared → volatility ↓ / equity breadth ↑ → easier market-based financial conditions; expiry can amplify or distort the signal.
catalysts.confirmation: Broad gains beyond mega-cap tech, contained VIX and a 10Y yield staying below the immediate post-Fed area would confirm durable relief.
catalysts.invalidation: A sharp expiry-session reversal with volatility and yields rising together would show Thursday's rebound was flow-driven rather than a genuine easing of financial conditions.

days.regime_label: Weekend Event Risk / 5% yields versus oil relief

catalysts.title: BOJ hikes to 1.25% by 7-2, but yen weakness shifts the next risk from policy surprise to intervention and carry volatility
catalysts.evidence: The Bank of Japan raised its policy rate from 1.00% to 1.25%, the highest in 31 years, with two board members dissenting. Instead of strengthening, the yen weakened and the dollar traded as high as 158.05 yen, while Japanese officials signaled readiness to respond to disorderly currency moves.
catalysts.transmission: BOJ hike + dovish dissent → yen weakness / intervention risk → carry funding volatility → JGB and global duration → equities and leveraged growth assets.
catalysts.confirmation: Further yen weakness with Japanese rate-check or intervention signals and firm global long yields would confirm that the policy move did not close the carry channel.
catalysts.invalidation: A sustained yen recovery accompanied by stable JGBs and lower global long yields would show that policy normalization is tightening funding conditions without destabilizing risk assets.

catalysts.title: U.S. 10Y closes at 5.01% while S&P and Nasdaq rise narrowly, creating a direct test of technology leadership versus the discount-rate ceiling
catalysts.evidence: Official Treasury data show the U.S. 10-year par yield at 5.01%, up 7bp from Thursday and 5bp from September 11. The S&P 500 still gained 0.17% and Nasdaq 0.40%, but the Dow and Russell 2000 fell and both NYSE and Nasdaq breadth were negative.
catalysts.transmission: 10Y near 5% → WACC and bond alternative rise → small-cap/cyclical breadth weakens → credit sensitivity increases → technology leadership becomes more fragile.
catalysts.confirmation: Monday reopening with the 10Y near 5%, weak breadth and continued Russell/Dow underperformance would confirm that Friday's index resilience is narrow rather than broad.
catalysts.invalidation: A sustained decline in the 10Y alongside improving breadth and small-cap participation would weaken the discount-rate ceiling thesis.

catalysts.title: China-Iran diplomatic intervention pushes oil lower, but Brent $104.87 and impaired Gulf routes keep the physical-risk premium alive
catalysts.evidence: Brent settled down 0.93% at $104.87 and WTI down 1.58% at $100.30 after China, acting on a Saudi request, asked Iran to limit Houthi attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure. Hormuz traffic remained far below normal and the Saudi East-West pipeline repair path remained uncertain.
catalysts.transmission: Diplomatic relief / repair progress → crude and fuel prices → inflation expectations → central-bank path and term premium → equity and credit valuations.
catalysts.confirmation: More Hormuz vessel traffic, verified Saudi pipeline capacity restoration and continued crude declines would confirm a durable easing in the physical premium.
catalysts.invalidation: Fresh attacks, delayed repair or renewed cargo cancellations accompanied by crude moving higher would show the diplomatic relief is temporary.

days.regime_label: Weekend Event Risk / policy relief versus 5% yields

catalysts.title: Bessent-He Sunday meeting puts AI security, trade, rare earths and the tariff truce directly in front of Monday market price discovery
catalysts.evidence: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng are scheduled to meet Sunday at JPMorgan's New York headquarters. Reuters reports the agenda includes artificial-intelligence security, trade and broader economic issues; separate reporting says rare earths and the tariff truce are also expected to feature.
catalysts.transmission: U.S.-China policy signal → AI/rare-earth supply expectations → CNH and semiconductor risk premium → global equity breadth and corporate capex.
catalysts.confirmation: A jointly described constructive agenda, no new restriction threat and firmer China-sensitive assets at Monday reopen would confirm a reduction in policy tail risk.
catalysts.invalidation: New tariff, export-control or rare-earth retaliation language that weakens CNH and semiconductor futures would invalidate the relief interpretation.

catalysts.title: China's policy debate shifts toward consumption and balance-sheet repair while September LPR is still expected to remain unchanged
catalysts.evidence: PBOC monetary policy committee member Huang Yiping said AI could deepen China's strong-supply/weak-demand imbalance and argued for consumption support, higher household income and balance-sheet repair for local governments and enterprises. Separately, all 21 respondents in a Reuters poll expected the one-year and five-year LPRs to remain at 3.00% and 3.50%.
catalysts.transmission: Consumption/balance-sheet support → domestic demand expectations → China equities and imports → industrial commodities and Asian growth assets.
catalysts.confirmation: Concrete fiscal or balance-sheet measures alongside stable credit conditions would confirm that support is moving toward demand repair rather than only lower policy rates.
catalysts.invalidation: No follow-through on demand support combined with continued weak household and corporate borrowing would leave the strong-supply/weak-demand imbalance unresolved.

catalysts.title: Saudi weekend attacks threaten to reverse Friday's oil relief before Gulf physical throughput is demonstrably restored
catalysts.evidence: Saudi Arabia's coalition said a ballistic missile launched toward Riyadh was intercepted and destroyed and that attempted attacks toward Yanbu, Taif, Baysh and Farasan were thwarted. Reuters and AP independently reported the escalation; the Houthis separately claimed attacks on sensitive Riyadh sites and an Aramco facility in Yanbu.
catalysts.transmission: Saudi security risk → export-route/freight premium → crude and diesel → inflation expectations → Treasury yields and equity discount rates.
catalysts.confirmation: Higher crude at reopening, new verified infrastructure damage or further attacks on Yanbu-related capacity would confirm that physical-risk premium is rebuilding.
catalysts.invalidation: No new damage, continued successful interceptions and further normalization of pipeline/Hormuz throughput alongside softer crude would weaken the escalation channel.

catalysts.title: Monday Asia opens risk-on in technology while U.S. front-end yields remain near cycle highs
catalysts.evidence: South Korea's tech-heavy index rose about 1.1%, MSCI Asia-Pacific ex-Japan gained 0.3%, S&P 500 futures rose 0.3% and Nasdaq futures 0.4%; Japan was closed for Silver Week while the U.S. 2-year yield remained around 4.7604%.
catalysts.transmission: AI demand optimism → chip/tech equities ↑; high 2Y/10Y yields → financing hurdle remains → breadth and small caps lag.
catalysts.confirmation: Broader Asian breadth, firmer European futures and declining U.S. 2Y/10Y yields would confirm the risk-on move is widening beyond technology.
catalysts.invalidation: A reversal in chip shares or U.S. futures while yields remain high would show the opening rally was a thin-liquidity sector move.

catalysts.title: Saudi export recovery keeps oil under pressure even as Houthi attacks and pipeline damage remain unresolved
catalysts.evidence: Latest Reuters Monday-Asia pricing showed Brent around $103.68 and WTI around $100.02 after earlier declines. Separate Reuters flow data showed Saudi exports recovering above 4 million bpd in September, with recent Hormuz shipments averaging about 2.9 million bpd versus roughly 0.7 million bpd in August.
catalysts.transmission: Saudi export recovery → crude/freight premium ↓ → inflation expectations ↓ → rate pressure eases → risk-asset discount rates improve.
catalysts.confirmation: Brent remaining near current levels alongside stable Saudi export volumes and no new infrastructure outages would confirm the physical-flow relief.
catalysts.invalidation: Fresh damage to Yanbu, Hormuz or the East-West route that cuts measurable shipments would restore the supply premium quickly.

catalysts.title: China holds LPRs at 3.00% and 3.50% as Bessent-He talks shift policy focus toward trade, AI and critical minerals
catalysts.evidence: China left the 1-year LPR at 3.00% and 5-year LPR at 3.50%, while U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng opened New York talks on the trade truce, AI guardrails, tariffs and critical-mineral flows ahead of a planned U.S.-China leaders' meeting later this week.
catalysts.transmission: LPR hold + U.S.-China talks → CNH/China credit expectations and AI supply-chain risk → Asian cyclicals, semiconductors and commodities.
catalysts.confirmation: Concrete language on critical-mineral flows, tariff-truce continuity or AI guardrails plus stable CNH would confirm reduced external tail risk.
catalysts.invalidation: No deliverables or renewed tariff/technology escalation ahead of the summit would leave policy risk largely unchanged.

days.regime_label: Selective risk-on / valuation relief with carry still tight

catalysts.title: Nasdaq closes at a record as SOX +4.3% and AMD crosses $1 trillion while the U.S. 10Y falls below 5%
catalysts.evidence: The Nasdaq rose 2.26% to 27,122.09, the S&P 500 gained 1.49%, SOX jumped 4.3%, and AMD rose about 10% as its market capitalization crossed $1 trillion; the official U.S. 10Y yield closed at 4.96%.
catalysts.transmission: 10Y yield ↓ + AI demand confidence ↑ → discount rate relief + semiconductor multiples ↑ → Nasdaq/SOX leadership → potential broader equity rotation.
catalysts.confirmation: Russell 2000 and cyclical breadth joining the rally while the 10Y remains below 5% would confirm broader financial-condition relief.
catalysts.invalidation: A renewed 10Y break above 5% with semiconductor underperformance or a sharp reversal in AMD/SOX would weaken the duration-relief thesis.

catalysts.title: Oil stabilizes near $100 Brent after Monday's selloff as Saudi export rerouting meets a possible U.S.-Iran diplomatic window
catalysts.evidence: Brent fell sharply on Monday and traded at $100.57 early Tuesday, while WTI October was $95.80. Saudi Aramco loaded roughly 14 million barrels on seven VLCCs near Ras Tanura on Sunday as Gulf exports recovered, while markets awaited any U.S.-Iran contact around the UN General Assembly.
catalysts.transmission: Saudi Gulf loadings ↑ + diplomacy probability ↑ → crude/freight premium ↓ → inflation impulse ↓ → long yields ↓ → equity valuation support.
catalysts.confirmation: Brent holding near or below $100 alongside continued Saudi Gulf loadings and no new major supply outage would confirm a lower physical premium.
catalysts.invalidation: A failed diplomacy window plus renewed Houthi/Saudi infrastructure disruption that pushes Brent materially higher would restore the inflation-risk chain.

catalysts.title: U.S. and China formalize an AI-safety dialogue and incident line ahead of the September 23–25 leaders' summit
catalysts.evidence: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the two sides agreed to a formal AI-safety dialogue, including an incident communication line, and plan to meet again in about two months in Shenzhen; the current tariff truce expires November 10 and no extension was agreed in the latest talks.
catalysts.transmission: Policy communication ↑ → AI/trade tail risk ↓ → semiconductor/supply-chain risk premium ↓; unresolved tariffs → CNH/exporters remain headline-sensitive.
catalysts.confirmation: Concrete summit language on AI protocols, trade stability or a tariff-truce extension would confirm lower policy tail risk.
catalysts.invalidation: New export controls, tariff escalation or failure to preserve the November truce would reverse the policy-relief channel.

days.regime_label: Selective risk-on / energy relief versus funding-cost constraint

catalysts.title: Nasdaq extends to a record close while the S&P stalls and the U.S. 2Y auction clears at 4.787%
catalysts.evidence: The Nasdaq Composite rose 0.45% to 27,244.28 and set another record close, while the S&P 500 was virtually unchanged and the Dow fell 0.36%. The official Treasury 2Y par yield ended at 4.71%, but a $69 billion two-year auction cleared at 4.787% with a 2.63 bid-to-cover ratio and a small tail to the when-issued level.
catalysts.transmission: AI optimism → Nasdaq leadership; restrictive front-end yield → funding hurdle → weaker breadth outside cash-rich technology.
catalysts.confirmation: Nasdaq leadership accompanied by improving Russell 2000 and bank breadth while the 2Y stays stable or falls would confirm a healthier broadening.
catalysts.invalidation: A renewed rise in the 2Y/auction clearing yields alongside Nasdaq reversal and weaker credit would invalidate the selective-risk-on setup.

catalysts.title: Saudi Arabia restarts the East-West pipeline as Brent falls below $100 and Hormuz diplomacy becomes a live supply catalyst
catalysts.evidence: Saudi Arabia restarted pumping through the East-West pipeline at a reduced rate after the September 11 attack, while full 7 million bpd capacity may take six to eight weeks to restore. Reuters also reported an Iranian offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week if U.S. military pressure and the blockade are eased. Brent traded around $99.92 and WTI around $95.33 in the latest retained global-market snapshot.
catalysts.transmission: Pipeline restart + potential Hormuz reopening → crude/freight premium ↓ → inflation expectations ↓ → long-yield pressure ↓ → broader risk-asset support.
catalysts.confirmation: Sustained Yanbu loading growth, Brent holding below $100 and verified progress on Hormuz access would confirm that physical-route risk is fading.
catalysts.invalidation: Fresh attacks, stalled pipeline throughput or failed U.S.-Iran diplomacy that pushes Brent rapidly back above recent levels would reverse the relief.

catalysts.title: Alibaba unveils its Zhenwu V900 AI chip while AI debt spreads widen, exposing the split between compute demand and financing cost
catalysts.evidence: Alibaba unveiled the Zhenwu V900 AI chip, said it is developing a 5–10 trillion-parameter model and targeted more than 20GW of data-center capacity by 2032. Separately, Reuters reported AI-linked corporate bonds trading around 115bp spreads versus roughly 78bp for the broader market, while SoftBank launched an $11 billion bond package to finance its OpenAI investment.
catalysts.transmission: AI model/chip demand ↑ → data-center capex ↑ → debt supply ↑ → credit concession ↑ → project hurdle rates and equity multiples become more financing-sensitive.
catalysts.confirmation: Continued AI revenue growth, successful bond absorption and stable or tighter AI-credit spreads would confirm that funding markets can finance the capex cycle.
catalysts.invalidation: Further spread widening, weaker primary-market demand or capex guidance cuts despite strong model demand would break the funding leg of the AI thesis.

catalysts.title: U.S. flash Composite PMI jumps to 58.4 as the 10Y reaches 5.11%, reversing the prior duration-relief trade
catalysts.evidence: S&P Global's September flash Composite PMI rose to 58.4 from 56.0, the highest since July 2021, while new orders, backlogs and input prices strengthened. The U.S. 10Y yield rose to 5.11%; S&P 500 fell 0.8%, Nasdaq 1.1% and Russell 2000 1.8%.
catalysts.transmission: Hot growth/prices → Fed path and term premium ↑ → 10Y/WACC ↑ → long-duration and funding-sensitive equity multiples ↓.
catalysts.confirmation: A sustained 10Y above 5% with Russell 2000 and non-cash-rich growth underperforming would confirm that the rate shock is binding across risk assets.
catalysts.invalidation: A decisive fall in the 10Y alongside better equity breadth, without a renewed oil spike, would weaken the growth-to-rates tightening thesis.

catalysts.title: The $70B U.S. 5Y auction clears at 5.033% with a 3.1bp tail, showing weak demand beyond the front end
catalysts.evidence: Treasury sold $70 billion of five-year notes at 5.033%, above the 5.002% when-issued yield. The 2.21 bid-to-cover ratio was below the recent six-month average of 2.33, and the on-the-run five-year yield traded near 5.023% after the result.
catalysts.transmission: Weak Treasury demand → term premium / 5Y yield ↑ → corporate and project financing spreads ↑ → capex hurdle and equity discount rate ↑.
catalysts.confirmation: Additional Treasury supply clearing with tails or low indirect demand while 5Y/10Y yields stay above 5% would confirm a persistent supply-driven financing premium.
catalysts.invalidation: Strong subsequent auctions with stop-throughs, higher indirect participation and a sustained yield retracement would weaken the Treasury-supply stress signal.

catalysts.title: Trump–Xi meeting on September 24 becomes the immediate trade, AI-safety and critical-mineral policy catalyst
catalysts.evidence: Xi Jinping is visiting the United States from September 23-25. Ahead of the leaders' meeting, U.S. and Chinese officials discussed an AI-safety notification mechanism, tariff treatment, trade and critical minerals, while several unresolved issues remained open.
catalysts.transmission: Trade/AI/critical-mineral outcome → tariff and supply-chain risk premium → semiconductors, CNH and cyclicals → global equity breadth.
catalysts.confirmation: An official joint or parallel announcement extending trade stability or formalizing AI-risk communication would confirm a policy-relief channel.
catalysts.invalidation: No verifiable progress, renewed tariff threats or tighter critical-mineral/technology restrictions would invalidate the de-escalation case.
